title: Lester at fourteen impresses a white band in Devil's Lake, North Dakota
summary: Phillips and Pete Jones always said nobody sounded like Bub; a fair bandleader offered Mr. Young 65 dollars a week for Lester, who refused as the boy was too young.

story.theme_name: Lester Young: the man, the sound, the Basie years
story.community_name: Remembering Lester Young: Prez the man and his sound

blocks.x: Because Pete and I used to say... Pete said, "You know one thing, Phil?" Said, "What, man?" "You know, we never run across nobody sounded like Bub on the saxophone, do we." I say, "We're sure don't." All the cats started moanin'. They wasn't runnin' over their horn playin' nothin', you know what I mean. Never did. And we went up in a lot of places. Went up in Devil's Lake, North Dakota, on this show. There was a White band up there. They had a little band up there, around six or seven pieces, and they heard Prez play -- he was on that show.
You mean Prez was playing with you at that time.
No, we was playing on his Daddy's show.
Oh, this was during the family band.
Yeah, on the show. On a carnival.

Yeah. So we was standing out on the bally, playing, and Prez was playing that horn. He was going over it. The guys was lookin' there, the musicians... See, they had a fair... Well, they had a platform out there, where they

had 10-cent dancing. You know, you'd pay a dime and go in and dance. Then they'd pull a rope behind you, and bring that crowd off, and another one go in. You'd dance about two or three numbers. Then they'd take that crowd off and bring in another one, and they had a band out there playing. But in those days, most of those fairs had little bands, like five or six pieces. Sometimes they had a big band. But man, this cat came and begged Mr. Young... He told him he'd give him 65 dollars a week, which was a lot of money then. You know what I mean? So he told him, no, he was too young. He wouldn't let him go out and play until he was about 16. He said, "Well, how did he learn to play all that stuff?" Old man said, "He learned it from his Daddy. You know, I play 'em all. I play all instruments, and I know..." "Oh, you're a musician." He said, "Sure."
